comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a robot-axis damper by unlocking, tuning, relocking, and testing repeated carriage stops; pr-1936 safely lowers and releases a stayed tool-chest lid.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key insertion, setscrew torque control, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and adjustment from dynamic response. pr-1936 requires sustained bimanual pulling and controlled lid lowering while avoiding pinch zones and excessive speed.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two physical cycles at ≥0.85 J within the specified velocity range, ≤12 mm piston travel, no hard-stop strike, rebound, overload, or lock drift. pr-1936 requires a shut, still lid, ≤0.15 m/s edge speed, released knob, withdrawn hands, and no pinch-zone entry. Candidate leaves rebound/overload limits and the final collar-drift tolerance undeclared; this does not make the unrelated lid outcome ambiguous.
comparison.reason: Both use bimanual stabilization and controlled articulated motion, but they test meaningfully different abilities: tool-mediated precision commissioning from repeated impact response versus continuously holding a safety release while lowering a hinged load.
